2026-10-23.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-10-23.name: Saint Ignatius of Constantinople
2026-10-23.story: Ignatius, born Nicetas about 799, was the son of Emperor Michael I. After his father was deposed he was shut in a monastery, where he embraced the religious life and became an abbot. In 847 he became Patriarch of Constantinople. He refused to help force the empress Theodora into a convent and rebuked the Caesar Bardas for repudiating his wife, and Bardas had him sent into exile. Restored in 867, he served about ten more years and died on October 23, 877.
2026-10-23.provenance: Brief story based on the Catholic Encyclopedia.
2026-10-23.sourceLabel: Feast source: Eparchy of St. Maron liturgical calendar

2026-10-24.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-10-24.name: Saint Arethas and Companions
2026-10-24.story: Arethas was an elderly Christian leader in Najran, a town in South Arabia and a center of Christianity there. Around 523, a local ruler besieged Najran and promised amnesty if the town surrendered. Arethas warned the people, but they surrendered. Arethas and many others, including priests, deacons, monks and consecrated virgins, were put to death because they would not deny that Christ is God. The Church remembers Arethas and his companions as martyrs on October 24.
2026-10-24.provenance: Brief story based on the New Catholic Encyclopedia, via Encyclopedia.com.

2026-10-25.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-10-25.name: Saint Chrysanthus and Saint Daria
2026-10-25.story: Chrysanthus and Daria were Roman martyrs buried on the Via Salaria Nova. Their tombs were publicly honored and their names appear in an early martyrology, so they were already venerated in Rome in the fourth century. A later legend says Chrysanthus was the son of a noble family of Alexandria who became a Christian in Rome, and that Daria, a Vestal, was won to the faith through him; it says both were stoned to death in a sandpit on the Via Salaria. The Catholic Encyclopedia notes that the surviving Acts have no historical value, but the martyrdom and the veneration of their tombs are certain.

2026-10-26.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-10-26.name: Saint Demetrius of Thessalonica
2026-10-26.story: Demetrius is remembered as a martyr and as the protector of the city of Thessalonica, in Greece. Catholic Online describes him as a deacon martyred at Sirmium and says early legends credit him with a military career. The Catholic Encyclopedia records that an oil said to work miracles flowed from his tomb. He was very popular in the Middle Ages.
2026-10-26.provenance: Brief story based on Catholic Online and the Catholic Encyclopedia.
2026-10-26.sourceLabel: Feast source: Eparchy of St. Maron liturgical calendar

2026-10-27.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-10-27.name: Saint Capitolina and Saint Erotheis
2026-10-27.story: Capitolina and her maidservant Erotheis were martyred in Cappadocia, in present-day Turkey. According to tradition, they died in the persecution under Emperor Diocletian, around 304. Their feast is kept on October 27 in the Catholic, Orthodox, Armenian and Syriac Orthodox calendars.
2026-10-27.provenance: Brief story based on Catholic Online and the Ecumenical Saints Lexicon.
2026-10-27.sourceLabel: Feast source: Eparchy of St. Maron liturgical calendar

2026-10-28.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-10-28.name: Saint Terence and Companions
2026-10-28.story: The Maronite calendar lists Terence and his companions on October 28. We have matched this entry to the group of martyrs Terence, Africanus, Pompeius and their companions, because the names fit; the calendar itself gives no details. According to Catholic Online, they were martyred in the persecution under Emperor Decius, and tradition says they were forced into a pit filled with serpents and stinging reptiles, and those who survived were beheaded. Catholic Online gives their feast as April 10, while the Orthodox Church in America lists Africanus, Terence, Maximus, Pompeius and others of Carthage on October 28.
2026-10-28.provenance: Brief story based on Catholic Online. The date follows the Maronite calendar.

2026-10-29.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-10-29.name: Saint Anastasia of Rome
2026-10-29.story: According to the Greek life of Saint Anastasia of Rome, she lost her parents at the age of three and was raised in Rome by an abbess named Sophia. During the persecution under Emperor Decius, the city prefect Probus had her arrested. She told him that Jesus Christ was her spouse, her riches and her life, and she was tortured and beheaded. This life was written long after her death, so the details come from tradition. Her feast is October 29 in the Orthodox and Byzantine Catholic calendars. She is not in the current Roman Martyrology, and she is a different saint from Anastasia of Sirmium, whose feast is December 25 in the West.
2026-10-29.provenance: Brief story based on Saints Encyclopedia. The date follows the Maronite calendar.

2026-10-30.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-10-30.name: Saint Macarius of Jerusalem
2026-10-30.story: Macarius was Bishop of Jerusalem from about 312 until his death, which came before the Council of Tyre in 335. He was one of the bishops whom Saint Alexander of Alexandria warned against the teaching of Arius, and at the Council of Nicaea in 325 his name appears first among the bishops of Palestine who subscribed. The chronicler Theophanes relates that after the council the emperor Constantine ordered Macarius to search for the sites of the Resurrection and the Passion and for the True Cross; the Catholic Encyclopedia notes that excavations in Jerusalem began very soon after the council, seemingly under his direction. The Maronite calendar keeps his feast on October 30.
2026-10-30.provenance: Brief story based on the Catholic Encyclopedia (New Advent). The date follows the Maronite calendar.
